answer: Shared-scarcity call pricing. Each agent call must reference a juniper unit drawn from a rate-limited regional pool sized to observed distinct demand, not to registrations. Identities sharing a network island or device crystal draw calls from one pool, so clones cannibalize the operator's own throughput instead of multiplying it. An attacker pays in lost capacity: every extra identity dilutes the pool, raising per-call latency and failure rate until the marginal clone yields less service than it consumes.
